newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Four killed in Belarus coach crash.
newsitem.headline: Four killed in Belarus coach crash.

text.p: Three young children from areas of Belarus affected by the Tchernobyl nuclear accident and a Russian teenager died when their Belgian coach overturned on a wet road, the company owning the bus said on Wednesday.

The dead were part of a group of over 300 children travelling to Belgian hospitals in a convoy of four coaches, all from the same Belgian company. The driver of the crashed coach was unhurt, director Joseph Cannaerts told Reuters.
Cannaerts, of the Excelsior company near Antwerp, said, "The driver explained...he couldn't avoid a car and the bus overturned. It is seriously damaged, lying near the road."

The crash, which happened at 5 P.M. Belarus time on Tuesday near the village of Kobrin, occurred in wet conditions and after a car skidded in front of the double-decker coach, a Belgian Foreign Ministry spokesman said.
Of the 70 children aged between seven and 14 on the crashed bus, three were seriously hurt and 60 had less serious injuries.
Cannaerts said the teenager who died was a 16-year-old Russian boy, possibly a translator.
The three seriously hurt children were taken to the clinic of Brest, near Kobrin.
The three other coaches would continue their journey on Wednesday afternoon and were expected to arrive in Belgium late on Thursday, Cannaerts said.

The whole group had been invited to Belgium by humanitarian Flemish association "Vlamingen helpen Tchernobyl kinderen", associated with "Medecins sans Frontieres". The accident at Chernobyl in Ukraine in April 1986 sent a radiation cloud over Belarus and other countries.
Many countries have been taking children from the affected regions to hospitals and rehabilitation centres abroad for medical treatment.
